# openvicloud_load_balancer (Resource)

An L4 (TCP/UDP) load balancer on a network with public IPv6. Name, listeners and backend VMs change in place and keep the VIP; another network replaces the load balancer (and gives it a new VIP). OpenViCloud refuses to delete a VM a load balancer still sends to: remove it from backend_vm_ids before replacing it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openvicloud_load_balancer" "web" {
  name           = "web"
  network_id     = openvicloud_network.web.id
  listener       = [{ protocol = "TCP", port = 80, target_port = 8080 }]
  backend_vm_ids = [openvicloud_vm.web.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `backend_vm_ids` (Set of String) 1 to 20 VMs of the same network.
- `listener` (Attributes Set) 1 to 10 listeners; a protocol and port at most once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--listener))
- `name` (String) Up to 100 letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or digit; unique in the tenant.
- `network_id` (String) A network with enable_public_ipv6; the VIP comes from its /64.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `vip` (String) IPv6 address the load balancer listens on.
- `cluster_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--listener"></a>
### Nested Schema for `listener`

Required:

- `port` (Number) Port on the VIP.
- `protocol` (String)
- `target_port` (Number) Port on the backend VMs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import openvicloud_load_balancer.web <load balancer id>
```
